questions.question: In causal language modeling (CLM), what probability distribution is the model trained to approximate?
questions.choice_A: The joint distribution over entire sequences, modeled non-autoregressively
questions.choice_B: The conditional distribution of each token given all previous tokens in the sequence
questions.choice_C: The marginal distribution of tokens independent of context
questions.choice_D: The posterior distribution of model parameters given the data

questions.question: Why is perplexity a useful metric for evaluating pretrained language models?
questions.choice_A: It directly measures semantic coherence in generated long documents
questions.choice_B: It approximates human judgment of text quality on open-ended tasks
questions.choice_C: It is a monotonic transformation of average cross-entropy, reflecting how well the model predicts held-out tokens
questions.choice_D: It measures the diversity of model outputs across random seeds

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes the difference between Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) and SentencePiece-Unigram tokenization?
questions.choice_A: BPE learns a fixed set of merges; Unigram models a probabilistic lexicon and selects a tokenization by maximizing likelihood
questions.choice_B: BPE supports byte-level inputs whereas Unigram cannot
questions.choice_C: Unigram requires whitespace-delimited languages; BPE does not
questions.choice_D: BPE optimizes tokenization using EM; Unigram uses greedy merges

questions.question: What is a primary motivation for training at byte-level (e.g., GPT-2 BPE with byte fallback) rather than strictly character- or word-level tokenization?
questions.choice_A: To completely remove the need for embedding layers
questions.choice_B: To ensure exact reversibility and robust handling of any Unicode text while maintaining reasonable sequence lengths
questions.choice_C: To guarantee shorter sequences than any other method
questions.choice_D: To make training stable without normalization

questions.question: When assembling large pretraining corpora like C4, WikiText, or RedPajama, what is the main reason for near-duplicate removal and deduplication?
questions.choice_A: To shrink the dataset so that overfitting is guaranteed
questions.choice_B: To remove all noisy data so that only curated text remains
questions.choice_C: To reduce memorization of repeated spans and improve generalization and evaluation reliability
questions.choice_D: To increase the average sequence length by dropping short texts

questions.question: Which property distinguishes AdamW from Adam in the context of training large language models?
questions.choice_A: AdamW drops the momentum terms entirely
questions.choice_B: AdamW decouples weight decay from the gradient-based update, improving regularization behavior
questions.choice_C: AdamW uses an adaptive learning rate per layer instead of per-parameter
questions.choice_D: AdamW requires no learning rate warmup

questions.question: What is the typical role of a learning rate warmup schedule in large-scale pretraining?
questions.choice_A: To decrease the batch size gradually to avoid overfitting
questions.choice_B: To increase the learning rate from a small value to the target value over early steps to stabilize optimization
questions.choice_C: To linearly decay the learning rate after a plateau in validation loss
questions.choice_D: To cycle the learning rate periodically for better exploration

questions.question: Why is effective batch size often measured in tokens (or token-sequences) rather than number of documents when training LLMs?
questions.choice_A: Documents are always the same length, so counting them adds noise
questions.choice_B: Token-level batches better reflect the actual number of predictions and gradient contributions per step
questions.choice_C: Token batching reduces the need for gradient accumulation
questions.choice_D: Token counts eliminate the need for padding

questions.question: Which benefit is most directly associated with mixed-precision training (e.g., FP16 or BF16) for LLM pretraining?
questions.choice_A: Guaranteed higher validation accuracy
questions.choice_B: Reduced numerical underflow without any trade-offs
questions.choice_C: Higher throughput and lower memory usage, often requiring loss scaling for stability (in FP16)
questions.choice_D: Elimination of the optimizer state memory

questions.question: What is gradient accumulation primarily used for in large-scale training?
questions.choice_A: To reduce variance by shuffling the dataset more often
questions.choice_B: To simulate larger effective batch sizes when GPU memory cannot hold a large batch in a single forward/backward pass
questions.choice_C: To reduce the number of optimizer steps to zero
questions.choice_D: To eliminate the need for model parallelism

questions.question: In causal language modeling, what is the main difference between training with full attention masks and prefix-LM (causal) masks?
questions.choice_A: Full masks allow each token to attend to all tokens, including future tokens; causal masks prevent attending to future tokens
questions.choice_B: Causal masks enable bidirectional context; full masks are unidirectional
questions.choice_C: Full masks are only used during inference
questions.choice_D: There is no difference; both are equivalent for CLM

questions.question: How does vocabulary size typically trade off with sequence length and model capacity in subword tokenization?
questions.choice_A: Larger vocabularies always reduce model size and sequence length
questions.choice_B: Smaller vocabularies increase sequence length but reduce embedding parameters; larger vocabularies shorten sequences but increase embedding parameters
questions.choice_C: Vocabulary size does not affect sequence length
questions.choice_D: Smaller vocabularies always increase training throughput

questions.question: Why is data contamination problematic when evaluating pretrained models on benchmarks?
questions.choice_A: It reduces training speed by increasing I/O demand
questions.choice_B: It causes inflated evaluation metrics because the model may memorize or partially memorize benchmark content
questions.choice_C: It prevents learning general patterns across domains
questions.choice_D: It breaks tokenization consistency across datasets

questions.question: What is a key insight from scaling laws regarding the relationship between parameter count, training tokens, and performance?
questions.choice_A: Performance depends only on parameter count once the model is big enough
questions.choice_B: Training tokens beyond a small threshold do not affect performance
questions.choice_C: There exists an approximately optimal trade-off between model size and number of training tokens for fixed compute
questions.choice_D: Compute budget is independent of tokens or parameters

questions.question: In the context of the Chinchilla-style findings, what happens when a model is undertrained in tokens relative to its parameter count?
questions.choice_A: It usually outperforms a smaller model trained on more tokens
questions.choice_B: It tends to be compute-inefficient and can show worse loss than a smaller model trained on more tokens
questions.choice_C: It exhibits the same validation loss as token-optimal models
questions.choice_D: It becomes more robust to distribution shifts

questions.question: Which learning rate schedule is commonly used after warmup for LLM pretraining to gradually reduce the learning rate?
questions.choice_A: Cosine decay, sometimes with a floor (minimum LR)
questions.choice_B: Exponential growth
questions.choice_C: Stepwise increases at each epoch
questions.choice_D: Randomized restarts at every batch

questions.question: Why is careful filtering (e.g., language ID, toxicity, document quality heuristics) applied to web-scale corpora like C4 or RedPajama?
questions.choice_A: To ensure the dataset only contains peer-reviewed text
questions.choice_B: To balance all domains equally
questions.choice_C: To improve data quality and reduce noise that can harm training stability and downstream performance
questions.choice_D: To avoid the need for deduplication

questions.question: What is the primary reason to use dynamic padding or packing when forming batches for CLM training?
questions.choice_A: To increase the model’s parameter count during training
questions.choice_B: To align sequence lengths so that computation is not wasted on padding tokens, improving hardware utilization
questions.choice_C: To ensure every batch contains the same documents
questions.choice_D: To keep the loss function convex

questions.question: Which statement about evaluation with perplexity is most accurate for research on pretraining?
questions.choice_A: Perplexity is fully predictive of downstream task performance across all tasks
questions.choice_B: Perplexity trends often correlate with many downstream tasks but may not capture abilities requiring long-horizon reasoning or instruction-following
questions.choice_C: Perplexity cannot be computed for byte-level models
questions.choice_D: Perplexity must always decrease linearly with training compute

questions.question: When reporting training progress for LLMs, why is it useful to track tokens processed in addition to steps or epochs?
questions.choice_A: Because epochs are not defined for streaming or sampled datasets, and steps can contain varying numbers of tokens
questions.choice_B: Because token counts directly measure GPU memory usage
questions.choice_C: Because token counts remove the need to specify batch size
questions.choice_D: Because token counts guarantee fair comparison across different vocabularies
